title: Caerlum Rising Again
premise: Jonah Fairweather, exiled for a storm-calling that killed her brother, has spent ten years in the valley of Caerlum where magic cannot follow — until the old gods stir and drag her back into a kingdom rotting from the crown down. A parasite god wears King Aldric like armor, feeding on prayers it now answers itself, and Jonah is the last storm-caller alive who can unbind him. Hunted by the king's own knights and shadowed by a found family of outcasts who keep choosing her over their own safety, she must decide whether truth or loyalty will save the realm. In the end she calls the storm she swore never to call again, tearing the god from Aldric at the cost of her exile's protection — and learns that justice outside the law still demands someone pay its price.
about_author: Wren Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing folk prayers in coastal parishes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people the law forgot, from a house that creaks like a ship.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ten years after her exile, Jonah tends goats in magic-dead Caerlum, haunted by the storm that killed her brother Tam. When a dying pilgrim crawls into the valley whispering that the gods are answering prayers again, his wounds knit with light no valley should permit. The beat: dread breaking through numbness.

chapters.title: A Prayer With Teeth
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The pilgrim's prayer was answered by something ancient and wrong; tracking its source, Jonah finds a shrine where offerings vanish upward. She meets Brannic, a disgraced knight sent to silence witnesses, who defects rather than kill her. The beat: reluctant alliance forged in mutual shame.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic reveals King Aldric hasn't spoken in his own voice for a year — courtiers call it piety, but Brannic saw the king's eyes go gold mid-audience. He shows Jonah the sealed royal chapel where prayers are harvested. The beat: horror of realizing the rot starts at the top.

chapters.title: The Company of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fleeing the capital's purge of storm-blooded families, Jonah gathers outcasts: Sefa, a child who hears god-speech; Maren, an apothecary burned for heresy; Old Ivo, keeper of forbidden rites. Around a smuggler's fire they become something like family. The beat: warmth earned through shared danger.

chapters.title: Storm-Blood
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren tests Jonah's blood and finds her power isn't dead — only sleeping, fed by grief. Flashbacks reveal Tam's death and the trial that exiled her. Sefa begins speaking in a voice not her own, naming Jonah 'the unbound one.' The beat: guilt confronted, identity cracking open.

chapters.title: The God Below the Chapel
chapters.summary: Old Ivo's POV. Ivo leads them through catacombs beneath the chapel to the god's root: a bound deity, Vessar, once worshipped justly, now twisted into a leech on Aldric's soul. Unbinding requires a storm-caller's oath sworn in truth. The beat: awe curdling into terrible understanding of the price.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The crown's inquisitor captures Sefa, demanding the company trade Jonah for the child. Brannic, torn between his old oaths and his new ones, betrays the inquisitor instead — but Jonah learns he once helped condemn her at trial. The beat: loyalty vs. truth colliding inside the found family.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Prayers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On the eve of the solstice rite, Vessar offers Jonah a bargain: her exile lifted, Tam's death undone, if she lets the king stay bound. She walks the capital streets hearing thousands of desperate prayers the god feeds on. The beat: temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Climax. In the chapel, before the assembled court, Jonah swears the true oath — confessing Tam's death as her own doing, not accident — and calls the storm she swore off. Lightning splits the binding; Vessar tears free of Aldric and is unmade by honest thunder. The beat: catharsis through costly truth.

chapters.title: Caerlum Rising Again
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Weeks later, Aldric rules in his own voice, the old gods answer honestly again, and Jonah — magic restored, exile voided — chooses to stay with her ragged family rather than return to glory. Sefa, learning to carry her gift, watches Jonah teach the first new storm-caller. The beat: quiet, chosen belonging.
